quarterly_data.signal: Investor Day 2026 (Singapore, September 29, 2026): Legrand raises its 2030 revenue and profitability ambitions. For 2027-2030 (subject to no major macroeconomic disruption): organic sales CAGR of +6% to +8%, plus an average annual scope effect from acquisitions of about +5%, with disposals over the period representing EUR 0,5 billion to 1,0 billion (French decimal commas as in source) of sales; average adjusted operating margin of 21% to 22% of sales after acquisitions and including restructuring costs; average free cash flow of 13% to 15% of sales, with cash conversion of net income above 100% on average. The company says it exceeded the growth and profitability commitments of its 2024 Investor Day and the strategic plan is fully in line with targets.
quarterly_data.figure: 2027-2030: organic CAGR +6% to +8%; acquisitions ~+5% a year; disposals EUR 0,5 billion to 1,0 billion (French decimal commas as in source) of sales; adjusted operating margin 21% to 22%; FCF 13% to 15% of sales

quarterly_data.signal: Data centers will represent more than EUR 3 billion of Legrand sales in 2026, built on strong organic growth and targeted acquisitions. Sales mix at end-H1 2026: data centers 32%, energy transition (electrification) 22%, essential building infrastructure 46% (incl. digital lifestyles). Data-center offering mix (end-2025): critical power 35% of data-center sales, physical compute infrastructure 25%, supervision / management / control of compute infrastructure 25%, advanced cooling 5%, testing and lifecycle services 10%.
quarterly_data.figure: Data centers > EUR 3 billion sales in 2026; 32% of sales at end-H1 2026; DC mix: critical power 35%, physical compute 25%, management/control 25%, cooling 5%, test/services 10%

quarterly_data.signal: Legrand unveils its data-center roadmap, including its vision of the transition to Low Voltage Direct Current (LVDC) architectures and a full roadmap designed to enable next-generation gigawatt-scale AI data centers; 'chip to grid' solutions and numerous innovations to be commercialized over the coming quarters. Market drivers cited: AI workloads, rising rack density, faster time to operation and new power-distribution architectures. A Malaysia case study (with Linkk Busway Systems) presents a regional data-center platform combining local production, engineering, project execution and recent acquisitions.
